subtitle: Hind ki Chadar: The Quiet Sword of Conscience at Delhi

panels.shot: solemn low-angle wide of Guru Tegh Bahadur standing calm before the distant domes of Delhi's imperial skyline
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur stands robed in simple white, hand resting lightly on a sheathed sword, eyes steady toward the unseen throne of Delhi, as the hazy outlines of Mughal domes rise behind him under a muted sky.

dialogue.text: Guru Tegh Bahadur, ninth Guru of the Sikhs, walks from Anandpur to Aurangzeb’s Delhi, choosing death rather than bend the conscience of India.

i18n.hi: सिखों के नौवें गुरु तेग बहादुर, आनंदपुर से औरंगज़ेब की दिल्ली तक चलते हैं, भारत की अंतरात्मा तोड़ने से अच्छा मौत चुनते हैं।

panels.shot: soft close-up on young Tyag Mal in a warrior encampment, lit by campfire glow
panels.action: A young Tyag Mal, later Guru Tegh Bahadur, sits by a dim campfire among weathered Sikh warriors, his face thoughtful as distant drums and tents hint at the battlefields of Guru Hargobind’s time.

dialogue.text: Born Tyag Mal in 1621, son of Guru Hargobind, he grows in a world of swords and psalms, where the Sikh path has already taken up arms against Mughal power.

i18n.hi: 1621 में त्याग मल के रूप में, गुरु हरगोबिंद के घर जन्मा, तलवार और कीर्तन की दुनिया में बढ़ता है, जहाँ सिख राह पहले ही मुग़ल सत्ता से टकरा चुकी है।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Tyag Mal in battle training, blurred motion of blade in foreground
panels.action: Tyag Mal practices swordsmanship in a dusty courtyard, his small frame controlled and precise as his blade arcs through the air, elder Sikhs watching with measured approval.

dialogue.text: He learns to wield the sword but turns inward, more drawn to silence than to acclaim; in time he will be called Tegh Bahadur, the brave of the sword.

i18n.hi: वह तलवार चलाना सीखता है, पर भीतर मुड़ जाता है; शोर से नहीं, चुप से लगाव। समय के साथ नाम पड़ता है — तेग बहादुर, तलवार का बहादुर।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Ganga plain with Guru Tegh Bahadur walking among common folk
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur walks barefoot along a village path on the Ganga plain, simple cloth wrapped around him, as peasants, artisans and wandering fakirs gather in a loose circle, listening in quiet respect.

dialogue.text: Long before Delhi, he walks the dusty roads of Punjab, Bihar, Bengal and Assam, singing of fearlessness and detachment, building distant sangats far from court.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली से बहुत पहले, वह पंजाब, बिहार, बंगाल, असम की धूलभरी राहों पर चलता है, निडरता और विरक्ति गाता है, दरबारों से दूर संगतें बसाता है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of the Guru seated in meditation, faint outline of Anandpur hills behind
panels.action: In a hut near the Shivalik hills, Guru Tegh Bahadur sits cross-legged in meditation, eyes half-closed, a faint smile on his lips as light filters through the thatched roof.

dialogue.text: In 1664, he is named ninth Guru; from the new town of Anandpur, he shapes a community that knows both the pull of devotion and the shadow of Mughal suspicion.

i18n.hi: 1664 में वह नौवें गुरु ठहरते हैं; नई बस्ती आनंदपुर से वह ऐसी संगत गढ़ते हैं जो भक्ति की खींच और मुग़ल शक्क, दोनों को जानती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Mughal court hall with officials in discussion, Guru Tegh Bahadur absent but implied
panels.action: Inside a Mughal provincial hall, officials in rich robes confer over scrolls and maps, a bearded clerk pointing to the Sikh regions in Punjab as a stern officer listens.

dialogue.text: Imperial eyes watch the Sikhs. Persian chroniclers will later call him rebel or bandit; Sikh memory will name him a shield. Both traditions agree on one point: the empire will kill him.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य की नज़र सिखों पर है। फ़ारसी इतिहासकार उसे बागी या डाकू लिखेंगे; सिख याद उसे ढाल कहेगी। दोनों मानते हैं: बादशाहत उसे मार डालेगी।

panels.shot: mid-shot inside Anandpur, Guru Tegh Bahadur addressing a small gathered sangat
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur stands beneath a simple awning in Anandpur, palm open as he speaks to farmers, women and soldiers sitting cross-legged, their faces lined with care and hope.

dialogue.text: His hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib speak against fear and tyranny, yet he does not raise an army now; his strength is a quiet refusal to bow before injustice.

i18n.hi: गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में उसकी बाणी डर और जुल्म के ख़िलाफ़ बोलती है, पर वह अब फौज नहीं उठाता; उसकी ताकत है ज़ुल्म के आगे चुप, अडिग इंकार।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Guru Tegh Bahadur listening to distressed visitors, faces indistinct to preserve historic ambiguity
panels.action: In a modest hall at Anandpur, Guru Tegh Bahadur listens as a small group of anguished men from the plains kneel before him, their clothing bearing signs of hardship, their faces blurred in the shadows of the room.

dialogue.text: Later Sikh tradition will remember pleas from persecuted Hindus and others, seeking protection for their faith; the earliest sources are silent on names, but not on the Guru’s choice.

i18n.hi: बाद की सिख परंपरा कहेगी, सताए गए हिंदुओं और दूसरों ने अपने धर्म की रक्षा को गुहार की; पुराने ग्रंथ नाम नहीं कहते, पर गुरु के फ़ैसले पर खामोश नहीं।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Guru Tegh Bahadur’s eyes as he contemplates, background fading to darkness
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur’s calm eyes fill the frame, reflecting a faint flicker of lamplight as the world behind him dissolves into darkness.

dialogue.text: Bachittar Natak will later declare: to protect the tilak and sacred thread, he offered his head. Whether for Kashmiri Pandits or all conscience, he resolves to stand.

i18n.hi: ‘बਚਿੱਤਰ नाटक’ बाद में लिखेगा: तिलक और जनेऊ बचाने को उसने सिर वार दिया। कश्मीरी पंडितों के लिए या सारी अंतरात्मा के लिए, वह ठान लेता है, डटेगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Tegh Bahadur bidding farewell at Anandpur gate, with faint suggestion of young Gobind Rai in background (not named)
panels.action: At the gate of Anandpur, Guru Tegh Bahadur turns back one last time, raising his hand in blessing toward a small boy and gathered Sikhs, the hills rising behind them under a pale morning sky.

dialogue.speaker: guru_tegh_bahadur
dialogue.text: No one truly dies who gives his head for truth.

i18n.hi: जो सच के लिए सिर दे, वह सच में मरता नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the road to Delhi with the Guru walking under a harsh sun, escorted by Mughal horsemen
panels.action: On a long straight road, Guru Tegh Bahadur walks in simple attire, hands loosely bound, flanked by mounted Mughal soldiers whose lances catch the heavy light of the afternoon sun.

dialogue.text: Arrested on the way, he is taken toward Delhi under guard. Dust rises around them; the empire believes it carries a troublesome saint to judgment.

i18n.hi: रास्ते में गिरफ़्तार, वह पहरे में दिल्ली ले जाया जाता है। धूल उड़ती है; साम्राज्य समझता है, एक झंझटू संत को क़ाज़ी के सामने घसीट रहा है।

panels.shot: establishing bird’s-eye view of Shahjahanabad with the Jama Masjid and Red Fort, tiny figures approaching
panels.action: From high above Shahjahanabad, the domes of the Jama Masjid and the red sandstone walls of the fort dominate the crowded lanes below, a small escorted group threading its way toward the heart of power.

dialogue.text: Delhi in 1675 is a city of marble and fear, where Aurangzeb rules with legal zeal, seeking to shape belief as well as law across his vast empire.

i18n.hi: 1675 की दिल्ली, संगमरमर और खौफ़ का शहर है; औरंगज़ेब कानून के जोश से हुक्म चलाता है, अपने विराट राज में आस्था भी क़ानून की तरह गढ़ना चाहता है।

panels.shot: shadowed interior of a Mughal prison cell, mid-shot of the Guru seated calmly
panels.action: In a dim stone cell, Guru Tegh Bahadur sits cross-legged on the bare floor, chains lying loose beside him as light from a small grated window draws a bright square on the wall.

dialogue.text: Sources differ on the words exchanged, but agree on the outline: a saint in chains, invited to save his life by surrendering his principles.

i18n.hi: वर्णन शब्दों पर अलग हैं, पर रूप एक सा: ज़ंजीरों में संत, जिसे कहा जाता है — सिद्धांत छोड़ दे, जान बचा ले।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Mughal official confronting the seated Guru in the cell doorway
panels.action: A richly robed Mughal officer stands at the cell doorway, one hand raised as if making an offer, while Guru Tegh Bahadur looks up at him, his face serene and unyielding.

dialogue.speaker: guru_tegh_bahadur
dialogue.text: A life bought by another’s enslavement is not worth keeping.

i18n.hi: दूसरे को गुलाम बना कर खरीदी ज़िंदगी, ज़िंदगी नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of the Guru reciting, hands loosely clasped, faint suggestion of script in the air
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur sits with eyes closed, lips just parted as if reciting, his fingers lightly intertwined, an aura of stillness around him in the cramped cell.

dialogue.text: His own verses speak within him: ‘He who fears none, and frightens none—why should he fall into dread?’ Fearlessness is his answer to the throne.

i18n.hi: उसकी अपनी बाणी भीतर बोलती है: ‘जिस को ना भय, न करै भयान — कहो नानक सुने चित्तु मान।’ सिंहासन के सामने उसका जवाब है – बेख़ौफ़ रहो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Chandni Chowk square, scaffold in the distance, crowd gathered in subdued tension
panels.action: In the open space of Chandni Chowk, a plain wooden platform stands under a gray sky, ringed by Mughal soldiers and a silent crowd whose faces hold awe, sorrow and curiosity.

dialogue.text: On 11 November 1675, he is led to execution in the marketplace of Delhi. No chronicle denies the end; they argue only about its meaning.

i18n.hi: 11 नवंबर 1675 को उसे दिल्ली के बाज़ार में फांसी को ले जाया जाता है। कोई इतिहास अंत से इंकार नहीं करता; बस मतलब पर झगड़ता है।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot from behind the Guru as he looks out over the gathered crowd from the platform
panels.action: From behind Guru Tegh Bahadur, we see his straight back and unbound hair as he stands upon the platform, gazing calmly over the vast, hushed crowd below.

dialogue.text: To some he is a traitor who defied imperial order; to his Sikhs and many others, he is Hind ki Chadar, the shield who offered his head so that conscience need not kneel.

i18n.hi: कुछ के लिए वह बादशाही हुक्म का ग़द्दार है; सिखों और बहुतों के लिए ‘हिंद की चादर’, वह ढाल जिसने सिर दे दिया ताकि अंतरात्मा घुटनों पर न गिरे।

panels.shot: poetic close-up of the Guru’s face tilted slightly upward, sky filling the background
panels.action: Guru Tegh Bahadur’s face is framed against an overcast sky, eyes lifted, lips set in quiet resolve, a faint breeze lifting the edge of his turban.

dialogue.speaker: guru_tegh_bahadur
dialogue.text: Let the body go; guard the truth.

i18n.hi: तन को जाने दे, सच की रखवाली कर।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot showing the scaffold silhouetted against the skyline, the act itself implied but unseen
panels.action: The scaffold stands in stark silhouette against the domes and minarets of Delhi, a bird taking flight from its beam as the crowd’s heads bow like a field of grain in the wind.

dialogue.text: In the stillness that follows, an empire has taken a life, but has failed to master a conscience.

i18n.hi: खामोशी के बाद, साम्राज्य ने एक जान ले ली, पर एक अंतरात्मा को वश में न कर सका।

panels.shot: dissolve-like wide shot of Anandpur, with the faint superimposed image of the Guru’s calm face in the sky
panels.action: Anandpur’s fort and houses lie under a clear dawn, Sikhs gathered in grief and resolve, while high above the town the faint, serene outline of Guru Tegh Bahadur’s face seems to watch over them.

dialogue.text: From this loss, the tenth Guru will forge the Khalsa, a community sworn to defend the weak. The death at Delhi becomes a living argument that faith must be free or it is nothing.

i18n.hi: इस खोने से, दसवां गुरु खालसा गढ़ेंगे — वह जमात जो कमज़ोरों की हिफ़ाज़त की सौगंध खाए। दिल्ली की यह मौत ज़िंदा दलील बनती है कि आस्था या तो आज़ाद होगी, नहीं तो मिट जाएगी।

title_i18n.en: Guru Tegh Bahadur Stands at Delhi
title_i18n.hi: गुरु तेग बहादुर, दिल्ली के द्वार पर

subtitle_i18n.en: Hind ki Chadar: The Quiet Sword of Conscience at Delhi
subtitle_i18n.hi: हिंद की चादर: दिल्ली में अंतरात्मा की खामोश तलवार
